# Ternuxx

Ternuxx turns Native Termux into a phone workstation managed with `tx`. Native Termux remains the host and control plane. Debian PRoot is an optional, separately previewed guest; installing the Native workstation does not create a Debian root filesystem.

## Install

From an attached Native Termux terminal, bootstrap the canonical checkout and open the managed installer:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx/main/install.sh | sh
# Alternatively:
wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/soobujmiah/ternuxx/main/install.sh | sh
```

The bootstrap prepares Git/locking prerequisites if missing and fast-forwards a clean
canonical checkout. It refuses unrelated or locally modified directories. Read
[install.sh](install.sh) before running it if you want to inspect the bootstrap.

Start the managed installer directly from this checkout:

```sh
./tx install
```

It shows device/system information and offers three profiles: **Minimal** (CLI, TUI,
Web UI, terminal/build tools, PRoot CLI provider and sound/graphics runtimes), **Native Full** (Minimal plus GUI management,
audio, graphics tools, selectable desktops/apps), and **Native Full + PRoot**
(the same Native selection plus one or more managed distributions). Use **Up/Down**,
**Space** and **Enter**; **Esc** cancels. `./tx install interactive` is an alias.

The wizard confirms repository preparation (`pkg update`, official X11 and Python
bootstrap), previews a separately confirmed system upgrade, and applies the exact
reviewed Native package selection. It also installs the checkout-backed `tx` shim.
Every guided profile includes the GTK management center and SSH/service management tools. Services start only through a separate explicit action. GPU backend selection is probed and
confirmed separately; installed drivers are not proof of acceleration. The matching
Termux:X11 Android app is installed/opened separately.

Native DEs are XFCE, MATE and Plasma; managed guests are Debian Trixie and Ubuntu
Noble. Select multiple DEs, apps or distros with Space. Guest usernames and hidden
passwords remain text inputs and are collected before bulk installation. A Writer-only Native package is unavailable; the
wizard does not substitute the monolithic LibreOffice suite. Guest setup offers
Writer-only and other optional apps after DE selection; the clean/base profile keeps
its managed CPU rendering, graphics and audio setup.

Later additions use `tx install xfce` (or `mate`/`plasma`) and
`tx install proot debian [DE]` / `tx install proot ubuntu [DE]`.
`tx install gpu` opens device-aware Native/PRoot/both runtime setup without requiring
a desktop. Guest selectors include a CLI-only option; current backend choices stay
the default, and a clean Native host gets a Zink recommendation only after a Vulkan probe. Existing guests get
preview-bound DE/app additions, preserving their rootfs and accounts.

The installer keeps device information, progress and elapsed time visible while its
content pane scrolls. It checks package state/free space and refuses a second guided
installer without stopping the first. Transient downloads have bounded retries;
integrity failures stop. See the guide for recovery and diagnostic details.

Automation retains `./tx install preview --profile NAME` and exact-plan apply;
see the [installation guide](docs/INSTALLATION.md).

```sh
tx doctor
```

## Open the workstation

Open the Floating Termux:X11 app, then start the Native desktop:

```sh
tx start
```

Manage the same Native workstation from the command line, terminal interface, authenticated loopback Web UI, or GTK center:

```sh
tx help
tx tui
tx web
tx gui
```

Each client exposes its supported operations through the shared management service. Review the [capability matrix](docs/architecture/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md) for current client coverage and open checks.

## Optional managed guest

Install a fresh, pinned Debian Trixie or Ubuntu Noble managed guest profile:

```sh
tx install debian
# or: tx install ubuntu
tx proot status
```

In an attached Native terminal, run `tx install debian` and follow the keyboard selectors. Ternuxx asks for the guest username, shows the pinned Debian target, and asks before installing. The normal setup uses XFCE and applies Ternuxx guest configuration, including available graphics setup and Native PulseAudio handoff. Existing guest data is preserved. Ubuntu Noble currently offers XFCE. Its standalone `:0` and guest-to-Native `:1` graphics routes passed live checks; nested `:2` starts XFCE and passes Vulkan/audio endpoint checks but remains partial because Xephyr DRI3/GLX drawing is unavailable. Other distro names remain unsupported until their Ternuxx-managed profiles are implemented and qualified. The separate `preview`/`apply --plan-id` commands are advanced automation and review forms; most users do not need them. The TUI can launch this guided installer from its terminal; Web and GTK provide distro selectors and open the guided installer in Native terminal sessions.

## SSH and services

`tx ssh inspect` reports Native SSH state. Ternuxx's managed service is designed for loopback port 8023 and uses preview-confirmed lifecycle changes. Unmanaged Native SSH configuration is outside Ternuxx service lifecycle control. Verify current configuration and listener evidence before enabling remote access; see [operations](docs/OPERATIONS.md) and [security](SECURITY.md).

## Troubleshooting

Start with read-only diagnostics:

```sh
tx doctor
tx status
tx proot status
```

If the Native package preview reports a missing X11 index, install the official `x11-repo` package and refresh package indexes as shown above. For graphics, recovery, audio, and service-specific checks, use the [task guides](docs/README.md).

Install the declared test dependency with `python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`, then run:

```sh
env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH bash scripts/repo_test.sh
bash tests/test_cli_help.sh
```
